headline: Medicare audit fears and an oil slump sink health care and energy while Amazon lifts discretionary; Nvidia's beat fades and tech barely gains
summary: SPY slipped 0.3% on Wednesday and the equal-weight RSP 0.2%; over the past month SPY is down 5.1% while RSP is down only 0.2%. Discretionary led (+1.8%), with tech, utilities and communication services up 0.3% and real estate 0.1%, while energy (−3.3%), health care (−2.2%) and financials (−1.1%) fell most. Over the month utilities (+4.0%), staples (+3.9%) and discretionary (+3.2%) lead, and tech (−11.7%), energy (−9.8%) and communication services (−4.2%) lag. Behind it: a second day of managed-care selling over CMS's proposed audit rule, a 3.2% drop in WTI on a surprise crude build, and Fed minutes showing almost all officials expect more hikes, though the 10-year eased to 5.07%.
drivers: Managed care drags health care for a second day

UnitedHealth fell 10.2% and Humana about 13%, with Elevance and Centene down about 7%, as investors priced wider Medicare Advantage audits and a renewed Medicare for All push; Merck (−3.9%) and Amgen (−3.1%) added to the drop. XLV lost 2.2% and its 1-month gain shrank to 0.7%, though it is still 13.4% above its 200-day. Oppenheimer called the selloff an overreaction, citing likely legal challenges to the rule.
Oil breaks lower and takes energy with it

WTI fell 3.2% to $83.26, its lowest since late August, after a 3.4m-barrel US crude build against a near-flat forecast. XLE fell 3.3% (Chevron −4.0%, refiners about −5%) and is now −12.5% month to date with RSI 28, its most oversold reading on the page.
Nvidia's beat fades; Amazon carries discretionary

Nvidia opened about 4% higher on its $130bn Q4 guide but closed −2.9% on leadership uncertainty, while AMD (+5.3%), Broadcom (+3.6%) and a 10% jump in Palo Alto left XLK up 0.3%. Amazon rose 3.8% as Anthropic's IPO, priced at $83 above its range, put a value on its stake, and beats at TJX and Target helped XLY to +1.8%.

The October minutes showed almost all officials expect further hikes, with a few open to 50bp in December if inflation disappoints; the cheaper oil still pulled the 10-year down about 4bp to 5.07%. That helped utilities, real estate and tech hold small gains while financials lost 1.1%.
rotation: The rotation map is unchanged for another session: tech in Lagging, energy in Weakening, communication services in Improving and the other eight sectors in Leading. No sector changed quadrant since Tuesday, but the leaders are thinning: health care's 3-month relative strength fell to +9.5 points (from +10.4) and materials is now 1.0% below its 200-day with only +0.7 points of relative strength, close to rolling into Weakening. Energy's relative strength is down to +0.7 points, one more weak week from Lagging. Discretionary is the one strengthening Leading sector (+6.4 points, 4.5% above its 50-day). The defensive rotation ends if XLK reclaims its 50-day average (11.8% above the price) with creations continuing and staples and utilities start to lose relative strength; Nvidia's fade means that signal has not come yet.
flows: State Street flows (to Nov 17) show tech dip-buying still building: XLK took in $985m in a week (0.9% of assets), $2.82bn in a month (2.6%) and $3.92bn over 3 months while its price fell 11.7% in a month, so ETF holders are adding into weakness rather than capitulating. Utilities saw the heaviest selling, −$894m in a week (3.8% of assets) and −$1.71bn in a month (7.4%) despite a 4.0% monthly gain, so that haven rally is being sold. Energy redemptions accelerated to $673m in a week (1.6% of assets) as oil slid, and financials lost $1.41bn in a month (2.7%) and $3.21bn over 3 months (6.1%). Health care added $962m in a month (1.9%) and materials $142m (1.7%). For scale, SPY took in $9.44bn in the week (1.2% of its $0.78tn) and $3.83bn over the month.
model: The six-factor model (12-1 month momentum 25%, 3-month relative strength 20%, trend vs the 200-day 15%, 1-month flows as % of assets 15%, forward P/E vs the S&P 500 15%, latest-quarter EPS growth 10%) still ranks energy first, but its score fell to 75 from 82 as redemptions hit the flow factor; health care is second (68), then staples (59), materials (52) and tech (51), which moved up to fifth past financials (50). Discretionary rose to 45 from 39, still eighth, on +6.4 points of relative strength. Communication services (31) and utilities (34) stay at the bottom, both dragged by month-long outflows of 4.4% and 7.4% of assets. Energy's lead rests on slow inputs (+55% 12-month momentum, 12.2x P/E, 151% Q3 earnings growth) while price, flows and RSI 28 point the other way, so I stay neutral. I also differ on financials (overweight, reading redemptions as under-ownership) and tech (more constructive than fifth given oversold conditions and steady creations).
weightsSrc: Schwab Center for Financial Research, as of Oct 2, 2026; rolled forward by each sector ETF's price change

XLV.view: Still the defensive leader on trend, but Medicare Advantage risk has moved from headline to price: UnitedHealth fell 10.2% and Humana about 13% on Wednesday after the CRUSH audit proposal and a renewed Medicare for All push, and Merck and Amgen also fell. XLV's 1-month gain is down to 0.7% from 5.5% two days ago. Pharma and tools carry less of this risk, and Barclays and Wells Fargo both favour the sector for 2027.
XLV.modelView: Second (68): +9.5 points of 3-month relative strength, the strongest trend (13.4% above the 200-day) and inflows worth 1.9% of assets in a month ($188m in the latest week). Weak spots are 9% Q3 earnings growth and RSI now 44.
XLV.trade: Hold the overweight through pharma and tools; avoid managed care until the CRUSH rule's comment period (to Jan 19) clarifies the audit exposure, and add only if XLV holds its 50-day average (3.0% below the price).
XLV.risk: The audit rule spreading to a wider Medicare Advantage squeeze; a tech rebound pulling money out of defensives.

XLF.view: A 10-year yield above 5% supports bank margins and capital-markets activity is strong; at 15.1x forward earnings the sector is about 83% of the market multiple. XLF fell 1.1% on Wednesday as hawkish minutes revived 50bp-hike talk, and it is only 0.9% above its 50-day. Wells Fargo cut financials to equal weight, while Morgan Stanley's Wilson still lists them among the cyclicals to add.
XLF.modelView: Sixth (50), down one place: +3.4 points of 3-month relative strength and 5.0% above the 200-day, held back by flows ($1.41bn out in a month, 2.7% of assets). The model scores that as a negative; I read it as under-ownership.
XLF.trade: Overweight; prefer large money-centre banks and brokers over regionals, and cut to neutral on a close below the 50-day average (0.9% below the price).
XLF.risk: Private-credit or commercial real estate losses; a flatter curve if the Fed hikes 50bp.

XLK.view: Nvidia's beat and $130bn Q4 guide did not hold: the stock closed −2.9% on leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit, though AMD, Broadcom and cybersecurity names rallied and XLK rose 0.3%. Software remains the weak spot after this week's AI-disruption selling. XLK is −11.7% over a month with RSI 29, earned 69% Q3 earnings growth and trades below the market multiple.
XLK.modelView: Fifth (51), up one place: second-best 12-month momentum (+31%) and strong valuation, earnings and flow scores (2.6% of assets in a month) offset the worst 3-month relative strength (−6.4 points) and a price 4.1% below the 200-day.
XLK.trade: Keep building towards benchmark in thirds: the first tranche is in; the second on a close back above the 50-day average (11.8% above), the third on a retest of the low that holds.
XLK.risk: Dip-buyers in the ETF capitulating if Nvidia keeps fading; software de-rating further around Anthropic's debut.

XLP.view: Staples slipped 0.3% on Wednesday but are +3.9% over the month on the safe-haven bid. At 23.7x forward earnings they cost about 30% more than the market, and Wells Fargo cut the sector to underweight for 2027. Walmart reports Thursday after beats at TJX and Target.
XLP.modelView: Third (59) on the strongest 3-month relative strength (+11.6 points) and trend (8.3% above the 200-day), with a weak valuation score. ETF buyers are late: $242m in the latest week but $158m out over a month.
XLP.trade: Neutral; trim into strength near RSI 65–70 (now 61) and rotate into pharma within health care.
XLP.risk: A deeper growth scare would extend the defensive bid.

XLE.view: The cheapest sector (12.2x) with the fastest earnings growth (151% in Q3 per FactSet), still +39.8% this year. But WTI fell 3.2% to $83.26 on Wednesday after a surprise 3.4m-barrel crude build, breaking the mid-$80s support I wanted held, and XLE dropped 3.3% to RSI 28. Gulf incidents are no longer lifting crude, and Morgan Stanley's 2027 view assumes lower oil.
XLE.modelView: First in the model (75, down from 82): valuation, earnings and 12-month momentum (+55%) carry it, but price (−9.8% in a month), flows ($673m out in a week) and the Weakening quadrant point the other way, which is why I don't follow the model's overweight.
XLE.trade: Neutral; don't add until WTI regains $85 and XLE recloses above its 50-day average (5.4% above the price); oversold readings alone are not a signal.
XLE.risk: Further surplus-driven oil weakness; Gulf escalation is the upside risk.

XLB.view: Materials are +12.7% this year on copper, gold and data-center demand, with about 30% Q3 earnings growth (FactSet). Wednesday's metal rout (gold about −3.5%, copper about −6%) hit Freeport and Newmont, and XLB is down 4.8% in a week and 1.0% below its 200-day with the dollar near a 19-month high.
XLB.modelView: Fourth (52), down from 55: 1-month inflows of 1.7% of assets and a positive 20-day money flow (CMF +0.08), but the trend is 1.0% below the 200-day and 3-month relative strength just +0.7 points.
XLB.trade: Neutral; wait for a close back above the 200-day before adding, and prefer data-center materials over miners while metals break down.
XLB.risk: A stronger dollar and slower China demand.

XLC.view: Down 9.5% this year and below its 200-day as investors question returns on Meta's and Alphabet's AI spending; FactSet shows the sector had the largest negative Q3 earnings surprise, though earnings still grew about 18%. It rose 0.3% on Wednesday. At about 18x forward earnings it is no longer expensive, and Wells Fargo upgraded it to overweight for 2027.
XLC.modelView: Last (31): flat 12-month momentum, 5.5% below the 200-day and $942m of outflows in a month (4.4% of assets). Valuation is the only positive; it stays in Improving on the rotation map.
XLC.trade: Neutral; a bounce candidate if tech turns, but it needs to reclaim its 200-day average (5.5% above) first.
XLC.risk: More capex without matching revenue; advertising slowing if the consumer weakens.

XLI.view: Industrials are down 8.2% over three months as the AI-power equipment trade unwound and trade at 22.5x forward earnings, a premium to the market. Strategists are split: Morgan Stanley's top sector for 2027, while Wells Fargo cut it to equal weight. XLI was nearly flat on Wednesday (−0.1%) despite Caterpillar's 2.1% drop.
XLI.modelView: Ninth (36): −4.1 points of 3-month relative strength, 4.7% below the 200-day and a poor valuation score. Flows are improving: $245m in a month after big creations last week.
XLI.trade: Underweight; keep aerospace and defence, and revisit electrical equipment only on a close back above the 200-day.
XLI.risk: A fast AI-capex rebound after Nvidia would lift the electrical-equipment names first.

XLY.view: Discretionary was the best sector on Wednesday (+1.8%) as Amazon rose 3.8% on the value of its Anthropic stake and TJX and Target beat; it is +3.2% over the month. But at 25.1x forward earnings it is still the most expensive sector and only +0.4% this year. Wells Fargo's overweight and Morgan Stanley's cyclical tilt are the case against my underweight, and Walmart and Black Friday are the tests.
XLY.modelView: Eighth (45, up from 39): +6.4 points of 3-month relative strength and 3.6% above the 200-day, but flat 12-month momentum and the weakest valuation score; $124m of creations in a month.
XLY.trade: Underweight for now; move to neutral if Walmart (Nov 19) and Black Friday data confirm spending and XLY holds 4.5% above its 50-day average.
XLY.risk: A strong holiday season or an Amazon-led re-rating forcing the move to neutral sooner.

XLU.view: Utilities rose 0.3% on Wednesday as long yields eased to 5.07%, and are +4.0% over the month as a haven. But the ETF is being sold into strength: $894m out in a week and $1.71bn in a month. Morgan Stanley is overweight on power demand; a December hike still caps the bond-proxy bid.
XLU.modelView: Tenth (34): weak 12-month momentum and the worst flow score (−7.4% of assets in a month), with RSI 56 and the price 0.8% below the 200-day.
XLU.trade: Underweight; use haven bounces to reduce.
XLU.risk: A bond rally if the Fed turns dovish, or a sharper risk-off move.

XLRE.view: The most rate-sensitive sector, with the Fed minutes pointing to more hikes. It edged up 0.1% on Wednesday as the 10-year eased and is +2.9% over the month; office and retail still face refinancing at much higher rates.
XLRE.modelView: Seventh (48): +1.6 points of relative strength, the best 20-day money flow (CMF +0.16) and $104m of creations in a month, but weak 12-month momentum and no valuation input.
XLRE.trade: Underweight the sector; prefer data-center and health-care REITs if exposure is needed.
XLRE.risk: A fall in long yields would spark a sharp short-covering rally.
